A block slides from Point P to Point Q along the track shown in Figure 1. The height $h$ of the track is indicated. A block is attached to three identical horizontal springs and rests on a horizontal surface, as shown in Figure 1. Frictional forces are negligible. When the block is at position $x=0$, the springs are at their relaxed lengths and the net force exerted on the block is zero. As the block is held at rest at various positions $x>0$, the net force $F_{s}$ exerted on the block by the three springs is recorded. Figure 2 shows lines $P$ and $Q$ that are possible best-fit lines for $F_{s}$ as a function of $x$. Which of the following indicates whether Line P or Line Q correctly represents the described scenario and provides a valid justification?

options.content: Line P , because as $x$ increases, all three springs exert forces of increasing magnitudes in the $+x$-direction.
Line $P$, because as $x$ increases, two springs exert forces of increasing magnitudes in the $+x$ direction and only one spring exerts a force in the $-x$ direction.
Line $Q$, because as $x$ increases, all three springs exert forces of increasing magnitudes in the $-x$-direction.
Line $Q$, because as $x$ increases, two springs exert forces of increasing magnitudes in the $-x$-direction, and only one spring exerts a force in the $+x$-direction.

Block A of mass 2.0 kg slides with a constant speed $5.0 ~m / s$ in the $+x$-direction on a horizontal surface toward Block B, which has a mass of 8.0 kg and is initially at rest. The blocks collide, and immediately after the collision Block A slides with constant speed 3.0 $m / s$ in the $-x$-direction and Block B slides with constant speed $2.0 ~m / s$ in the $+x$-direction. Which of the following claims regarding whether the collision is elastic or inelastic is correct and provides a valid justification?

options.content: The collision is inelastic because the blocks have unequal masses.
The collision is inelastic because momentum is conserved in the collision but kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
The collision is elastic because the blocks move in opposite directions after the collision.
The collision is elastic because both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved in the collision. 12 Mark for Review
